messages:
maria (Marketing PM): Heads-up — we're finalizing the benchmark narrative for next week's launch. Need two things by EOD: (1) the final chart set for latency vs cost that we use in the blog + slide deck, and (2) a simple inbound routing plan so SDRs can act on high-intent demo leads. Quick sync?

alex (Content): On charts — can we avoid the standard scatterplot-only approach? I want a 3-frame visual: overview scatter (cost vs median latency), a small-multiples of latency distributions for 3 customer slices, and a single-slide ROI calc for a sample 1M-token/week app. :sparkles:

jamie (Product Marketing): Agree with alex. For the small-multiples have rows = model variants (quantized vs fp16) and cols = request profile (short chat, long completion, embedding batch). Keeps it concrete. Use percentile bands (P50/P95) not just mean.

ryan (Growth): For inbound routing, simple rule: if a trial customer views the benchmark blog and uses our pricing calc -> mark as "bench-engaged". If they also request higher throughput in console or ping sales chat, escalate to SDR with attached benchmark snapshot. We can automate an initial lead score: viewed_doc + run_calc + >1k tokens in trial => lead.

maria (Marketing PM): Nice. Need copy hooks for blog and email subject lines. Two options: one technical (latency-first) and one business (cost-econ). Drafts?

alex (Content): Technical subject: "How we shave 40ms off 95th percentile latency — and why it matters". Business subject: "Reduce LLM per-token cost by up to 3x for production workloads".

jamie (Product Marketing): For the ROI slide text: short bullet: "Example: a conversational UX with 2k tokens/session, 50k sessions/mo — switching to Redwood-optimized serving reduces infra cost by X and 95th latency by Y, unlocking 2x session throughput." Put numbers in a single table cell, not paragraphs.

ryan (Growth): For routing mechanic — minimal payload that goes to SDRs: customer id, page viewed (benchmark article url), calc result, trial token volume, and suggested play (demo vs technical deep-dive). We'll wire it to Intercom/Zendesk.

bench-bot: [automated perf summary] Generated sample dataset for visuals: models=['rw-13b-fp16','rw-13b-q4','rw-7b-q4'], profiles=['chat-short','completion-long','embeddings-batch'] — median/95 samples attached.

maria (Marketing PM): Alex, can you draft 3 chart PNGs using the bench-bot sample by noon? Jamie, can you produce the one-slide ROI calc (numbers + short rationale)? Ryan, can you draft the webhook payload spec for SDR routing? I'll stitch and run copy tests.

alex (Content): On it. Couple quick asks: (a) let's annotate the scatter with a simple callout: "real customers run at P95 latencies, not mean" and (b) add a tiny inset showing per-token $ cost assumptions (batch size, GPU type).

jamie (Product Marketing): I'll do ROI + a one-paragraph talking point for the blog that ties latency improvements to user retention. Keep it <70 words.

ryan (Growth): Draft payload for SDRs (example):
```
{
  "customer_id": "1234",
  "event": "benchmark_article_viewed",
  "calc_result": {"estimated_monthly_tokens": 1000000, "monthly_cost_red": "~$X"},
  "trial_token_usage": 12000,
  "suggested_play": "technical-demo"
}
```
I'll push this to the routing doc and add a Zap -> Intercom flow.

maria (Marketing PM): Perfect. A couple of UX/positioning notes for the draft blog: lead with a short customer-story style opener (30-40 words), then show the three visuals. Avoid heavy claims like "best" — instead say "typical improvements we see when customers adopt our serving defaults".

alex (Content): For CTAs: (1) interactive pricing calculator, (2) sign-up for benchmark webinar, (3) request a dedicated benchmarking session. For the webinar blurb: 30-min technical session, demo of the visualization + Q&A with infra team.

jamie (Product Marketing): Webinar angle — "Decoding inference economics: what product teams should optimize for". Emphasize tradeoffs and decision heuristics (when to quantize, when to add cache). Keep it pragmatic.

ryan (Growth): I'll wire a landing page variant that captures which CTA they clicked. Bench-engaged leads get a custom tag and a follow-up sequence: 24h email with ROI snapshot, 3-day SDR nudge if calc_result > threshold.

maria (Marketing PM): Final asks before EOD: alex -> chart PNGs + suggested alt text; jamie -> ROI slide + 70-word paragraph; ryan -> routing spec + Intercom zap notes. I'll assemble and share a final staging link. Anyone object to this plan?

alex (Content): No objections. Quick note — for accessibility, include text-only table of numbers under each chart.

jamie (Product Marketing): Good call. Also recommend a short A/B test on the blog hero: technical vs business subject lines. We can measure CTR -> calc run rate.

ryan (Growth): Agreed. I'll add UTM params for each variant.

maria (Marketing PM): Thanks team. If you run into missing bench numbers ping bench-bot with `/bench regenerate profile=chat-short` and it should spit a fresh sample. I'll loop in design if we need iconography. :rocket:

bench-bot: Command acknowledged. New sample scheduled for 1893456870.
